diagnosis_explanation: You had surgery to replace your right knee. This was done because your knee joint had wear and tear. This surgery is often called a total knee replacement. Your knee should feel much better now.
medication_rationale:
Celebrex 200 mg:
This medicine helps reduce pain and swelling. It is used after your knee surgery. You should feel less pain in your knee. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you have stomach pain, black stools, or vomit blood.

Colace 100 mg:
This medicine helps soften your stools. It makes it easier to have a bowel movement. You will notice your stools are softer. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain or cramping.

Protonix 40 mg:
This medicine reduces stomach acid. It can help prevent stomach problems from other medicines. You may notice less stomach upset. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain or trouble swallowing.

Synthroid 137 mcg:
This medicine replaces a hormone your thyroid gland makes. It helps control your body's energy. You should feel more energetic and less tired. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you have a fast heartbeat, feel nervous, or have trouble sleeping.

Diprosone cream 0.05%:
This cream helps reduce redness and itching. It is for your right arm and right abdomen. The skin on your arm and abdomen should look and feel better. This means the cream is working. Call your doctor if the skin becomes more red, itchy, or burns.

oxycodone SR 20 mg:
This medicine is a strong pain reliever. It is for moderate to severe pain after your surgery. You should feel your pain lessen. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you feel too sleepy, have trouble breathing, or are unable to urinate.

Percocet 5/325 mg:
This medicine is a pain reliever. It is for sudden, sharp pain that may occur. You should feel your breakthrough pain get better quickly. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you feel too sleepy, have trouble breathing, or are unable to urinate.

Trazodone 50 mg:
This medicine can help you sleep. It is for short-term use after your surgery. You may fall asleep more easily at night. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you feel very restless or agitated.

Ativan 0.25 mg:
This medicine can help reduce anxiety. It is for short-term use after your surgery. You may feel calmer and less worried. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you feel very drowsy or have trouble thinking clearly.

Toprol-XL 50 mg:
This medicine helps control your heart rate and blood pressure. It is used for your heart condition. You may notice your heart beating slower. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you feel dizzy, tired, or have trouble breathing.

Coumadin 7 mg:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots from forming. This is important after your surgery. You may not notice any changes. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you notice any unusual bleeding or bruising.
Important: Do not stop taking this medicine without calling your doctor first.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and may have some pain in your knee.
- Keep your surgical leg straight when resting.
- Use the CPM machine as directed by your therapist.
- Walk short distances inside your home.
- Do not bend your new knee more than 90 degrees.
- Do not put any weight on your surgical leg.
- You may drive if you are not taking pain medicine.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101°F.
- Your goal is to do all your exercises every day.

**Week 2:**
- Your knee pain should start to get a little better.
- You will feel more energy than last week.
- Continue CPM machine use as directed.
- You can put light weight on your surgical leg.
- Try to walk a bit more inside your home.
- Do not bend your knee past 90 degrees.
- Call your doctor if you see redness or swelling at the incision.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel less pain and more comfort.
- You can start doing more activities around the house.
- Continue physical and occupational therapy sessions.
- You can begin to put full weight on your surgical leg.
- Keep bending your knee to 90 degrees.
- You can drive again if you are not taking pain medicine.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes.
- Call your doctor if your calf pain gets worse.

**Week 4:**
- Your knee should feel more stable and less swollen.
- You can walk longer distances without pain.
- You can start doing light chores around your home.
- Continue exercises and therapy as planned.
- You may increase bending your knee slowly.
- Ask your doctor before going back to work.
- Your goal is to walk outside for short periods.
- Call your doctor if your surgical leg feels numb or tingly.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should see steady progress over the next few weeks.
- Keep up with your therapy exercises daily.
- Manage your pain with the medications prescribed.
- Listen to your body and rest when you need to.
- Most people return to normal activities in 6 weeks.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Severe pain not helped by medicine: Your pain is too bad.
- Leg swells badly with pain: You may have a blood clot.
- Wounds look infected: Red streaks or pus mean trouble.
- You cannot keep fluids down: You may get too dry.
- You feel very confused: This can be a serious sign.
- You fall and get hurt: You need a check right away.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that slowly gets better: This is normal healing.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen after surgery.
- Wound healing slower than expected: Check for infection signs.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can explain doses.
- Mild redness not spreading: This is often not serious.
- Waking often at night: Pain or anxiety can disrupt sleep.
- Constipation that is mild: Your body is adjusting slowly.
- Rash from gardening: Your skin is healing from contact.
